novelty_flags.label: related_work; literature_map; comparator promise for LeeWeidner2026
novelty_flags.one_line: The cited Journal of Econometrics version places Theorem 1 and Proposition 1 in the two-observation/second-order construction; arbitrary-order bounds are developed in Section 4, so these anchors do not support the claimed generic order-m comparator.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 256, Part A, July 2026, article 106254
source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, Theorem 1 and Proposition 1; Section 4, arbitrary-order extension
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 and Proposition 1 establish the two-observation/second-order limited-pooling construction; the paper separately extends the method to arbitrary order in Section 4.
Wood studies the convex geometry of fixed-binomial mixtures, gives convergence results in Theorems 1–2, and uses Example 2 for a nonidentifiable mixture slice.
For compact generalized moment problems with relative-interior moment data, the paper establishes dual attainment; its applications are not hierarchical causal ATE fibers.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics 35(2), 2026, pp. 880–890
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article constructs exact pointwise confidence intervals for CDFs and quantiles of an unrestricted univariate binomial mixing distribution by inversion of composite tests.
Bugni develops bootstrap inference for partially identified models defined by finitely many weak moment inequalities, targeting coverage of the identified set.
The work concerns DOT treatment effects with individual observations across Brazilian cities and discusses latent local-level random effects in propensity and outcome modeling.
The paper studies CAD with equational constraints as a real quantifier-elimination method, rather than a causal finite-support reduction.
